about: A loader that copies a pod into a GraphDB server, so that a developer can explore the pod's records with GraphDB's own tools. npm run graphdb -- <name> <GraphDB's base URL> runs it; no app needs it.
capabilities: Loading a pod into GraphDB · load(), GraphDB
Asking a GraphDB repository a question · GraphDB.ask()

glossary.definition: a query a lens carries that works out statements from a pod's files which the files do not hold themselves; what the derivations of a lens work out is the pod's derived state under it.

what a lens works out from a pod's files and keeps beside them: statements the files do not hold themselves. It is kept in a graph of its own, named for the lens (`urn:cascade:derived:<lens>`), apart from the files.
Ontotext's database for data written as statements, with a web workbench for browsing and querying it.
a choice of which judgments count when a question is answered: `everyday` is the default, and `export` is stricter, for records sent elsewhere.
a set of statements kept under a name, an IRI, inside one store; a query can ask which graph a statement is in.
a query the vocabulary carries under a name, such as `pod/My active allergies`.
one person's records, and what that person has said about them, kept as files in one folder.
one thing said about a person's health, such as an allergy, a medication or a lab result.
one database on a GraphDB server, with an ID and a title.
one line of a table: of a view, what one view entry holds, a cell per column; of a reference table, what it says of one code or variant.
a SPARQL query that GraphDB keeps under a name, for anyone using the server to run.
the W3C query language for data written as statements, as Turtle writes them; `pod.ask()` runs an app's own SPARQL SELECT.
